answer: A decentralized economy of AI agents can resist fake-identity attacks through the use of a Sybil-resistance mechanism based on a hierarchical voting system. In this system, each agent's vote is mirrored by a corresponding vote from a trusted anchor agent, creating a plume of verifiable votes that converge at the summit of the voting consensus. This approach renders it costly for an attacker to create fake identities, as they must now create multiple anchor agents to support a single fake identity, thereby increasing the computational and resource costs of a Sybil attack.
